clue.text: Country's official certificate presented to immigrant finally

parts.note: a diploma is a certificate awarded for passing a course

indicators.note: finally asks for the closing letter of the word immigrant

explanation.surface: A government officer hands a certificate to a newly arrived immigrant at the end of the process.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country's official' reads as a describing phrase, but the whole phrase is the definition: an envoy who represents a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: An envoy representing a nation abroad is that state's official in a foreign capital.

clue.text: Prevalent, like lice for Cockney?

explanation.surface: A Cockney describes where head lice live.
explanation.walkthrough: Lice live in the hair; a Cockney (Londoner) drops the H, saying in 'air.
explanation.definitionFit: Something widespread is felt all around, as an atmosphere; lice dwell among the strands of a scalp, said without an H.

clue.text: Ground endlessly needing money, leading to anger in county cricket team

indicators.note: endlessly means the word for ground loses its final letter

parts.note: land means ground
cash is money
ire is anger

explanation.surface: A cricket club's ground keeps needing money, which makes everybody furious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts LAND to LAN. Lancashire is an English county with a first-class cricket side.
explanation.definitionFit: A first-class English cricket side is named after the north-west county it represents.

clue.text: Collection of items is brought to room — lots to be left outside

indicators.note: to be left outside says the word for lots stays on the outside, around the other pieces

parts.note: many means lots
a cell is a small room

explanation.surface: Assorted items are brought into a room, while a pile is left outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be left outside' wraps the word for lots around the rest; 'brought to' only joins IS to the room, and the dash hides that the clue's second half is still wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An assortment of various things gathered together, such as a mixed anthology.

clue.text: After drink band becomes violent

indicators.note: after says the word for band follows the word for drink

parts.note: tea is a drink
a ring is a band

explanation.surface: After drinking, a group of musicians turns aggressive.
explanation.definitionFit: A tearing wind or hurry is furious and forceful.

clue.text: Plans drawn up for mass mailing

indicators.note: drawn up in a down clue means the word for plans is read from bottom to top

parts.note: maps are plans or charts

explanation.surface: Plans are prepared for a bulk mailshot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawn up' reverses MAPS in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Unwanted bulk email sent to many recipients at once.

clue.text: Bill takes line to achieve agreement

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill
a cord is a line or string

explanation.surface: A parliamentary bill is amended with a line of text to reach consensus.
explanation.walkthrough: AC (account) for 'Bill' is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Harmony or a pact between parties is a meeting of minds.

clue.text: He gets ogre destroyed

indicators.note: destroyed means the letters of gets and ogre are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A hero has a monster killed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'destroyed' rearranges GETS OGRE; read whole, the clue describes the dragon-slaying patron saint of England.
explanation.definitionFit: England's patron saint is famed for slaying a dragon, a monster like an ogre.

clue.text: Plain old lover — initial touch of powder permitted?

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

indicators.note: the initial touch of a word is just its opening letter, here of powder

parts.note: licit means lawful or permitted

explanation.surface: A former partner applies a first dab of make-up, wondering whether it is allowed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something stated plainly is spelt out clearly, leaving nothing implied.

clue.text: Get cramps in publicity events maybe

explanation.surface: Someone at a series of promotional events is seized by painful cramps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get ... in' frames the two definitions: find a word for cramps in a word for publicity events. Stunt as a verb means to check growth.
explanation.definitionFit: To cramp something is to hold back its development, as stunting does; publicity events are attention-grabbing feats staged for the press.

clue.text: Biological structure medic in old style kept in metal plate

indicators.note: kept in tells us one piece is held inside the word for metal plate

parts.note: chrome is a plating of chromium on metal

indicators.note: in says the word for medic sits inside the old style abbreviation

parts.note: OS is the abbreviation for Old Style, the calendar dating used before 1752
MO is a medical officer, a military doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor in an old-fashioned style is preserved in a metal plate, like an exhibit.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers nest here: 'in' and 'kept in' each signal one, so read 'medic in old style' as a unit before placing it in the plating word.
explanation.definitionFit: A thread of DNA carrying genes inside a cell nucleus is a structure studied in biology.

clue.text: Left to go to a very large country

parts.note: OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize, very large

explanation.surface: Someone leaves to travel to a huge nation.
explanation.walkthrough: OS (outsize) is a clothing-size label for very large garments.
explanation.definitionFit: A landlocked nation in Southeast Asia, bordering Vietnam and Thailand.

clue.text: Someone with an estate such as Bill Andrews?

explanation.surface: A man named Bill Andrews is given as an example of a property owner.
explanation.walkthrough: The name Bill Andrews holds the letters L AND in its middle (bilL ANDrews), so the name itself is a holder of land: the second definition is a pun.
explanation.definitionFit: An estate owner holds property; the name in the second reading physically contains the letters of a word for ground.

clue.text: Pansy's condition unlikely to cause palpitations

explanation.surface: A pansy's state of health is described as calm and steady.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', joining the two definitions; heartsease is a wild pansy.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild viola flower bears the name; a calm cardiac state, read as two words, would not set the pulse racing.

clue.text: Insincere worship with silly spiel — rector's principal shortcoming

indicators.note: silly suggests the letters of spiel are jumbled foolishly
principal asks for the leading letter of rector's

parts.note: a vice is a moral shortcoming

explanation.surface: A vicar's hollow sermon is criticised as his main failing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'silly' rearranges SPIEL into LIPSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Paying devotion with words alone, without genuine feeling, is empty respect.

clue.text: Perhaps the M25 section that gets spoken about

indicators.note: about tells us the word for spoken goes around the word for section

parts.note: oral means spoken rather than written
a bit is a section or piece

explanation.surface: A stretch of a London motorway is a part people talk about.
explanation.walkthrough: The M25 is the motorway ringing London, known as the London Orbital.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring road circling a city follows a loop around it, as the M25 does around London.

clue.text: Waiting for a delivery, maybe, but not actually working

explanation.surface: Someone awaits a parcel at home, though they are not really at work.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the batsman facing the bowler is the striker, waiting for each ball (delivery); 'delivery' tempts a reading about parcels or childbirth.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket batsman facing the bowler awaits the next ball; workers in an industrial dispute have walked out.

clue.text: To make medical assessment, touching friend's head

parts.note: a pal is a friend; the 's simply joins on the next piece
pate is an old word for the head

explanation.surface: A doctor's examination involves touching a friend's head.
explanation.definitionFit: Doctors examine by feeling the body with their hands, a hands-on diagnostic check.

clue.text: Dish prepared with strange rite involving one wild ox

indicators.note: involving says the rearranged rite letters surround the other pieces
strange means the letters of rite are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a yak is a wild ox of Tibet

explanation.surface: A meal is cooked during an odd ceremony featuring a wild ox.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared with' looks like an anagram signal but is a link; 'strange' makes TERI, and 'involving' wraps that round one plus the ox.
explanation.definitionFit: A Japanese preparation of meat or fish glazed in a sweet soy marinade and grilled.

clue.text: Seeing that charity commanding support, be at the forefront

indicators.note: at the forefront says the word be goes in front of the other piece

parts.note: a cause is a charity or movement that people support

explanation.surface: A charity with backing should be leading the way.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are conjunctions giving a reason, meaning since or as.

clue.text: Restriction on motorists making any journeys

definitions.text: Restriction on motorists making any journeys

parts.words: Restriction on motorists making any journeys
parts.note: reads like a law limiting driving, but describes the strap that physically restrains a driver on every trip

explanation.surface: A rule limits motorists from travelling at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Restriction' suggests a regulation; it is a literal restraint across the body worn on every car journey.
explanation.definitionFit: A strap holding car occupants in their seats restrains them on each trip.

clue.text: Deprivation at home which celebrity goes round

indicators.note: goes round tells us the word for celebrity encircles the other piece

parts.note: fame is celebrity
in means at home

explanation.surface: A famous person drops by a home suffering hardship.
explanation.definitionFit: A severe shortage of food leaves a population starving and in want.

clue.text: Prophet appearing as the ultimate character in a particular period

indicators.note: in tells us the last character is put inside the word for period

parts.note: an era is a particular period of history
Z is the last letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A prophet emerges as the defining figure of his age.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hebrew scribe and priest with an Old Testament book named after him is counted among the prophets.

clue.text: Another wedding? Reg and Irma are getting excited

indicators.note: getting excited suggests these letters are stirred up into a new order

explanation.surface: Reg and Irma are thrilled about tying the knot again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting excited' rearranges the letters of REG, IRMA and ARE; 'and' only joins the names.
explanation.definitionFit: Marrying for a second time is a further wedding ceremony.

clue.text: Agitator to lose heart and wobble

indicators.note: to lose heart means the middle letter of the word for agitator is dropped

parts.note: a rebel is an agitator

explanation.surface: A troublemaker becomes discouraged and starts to waver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to lose heart' removes the central B from REBEL.
explanation.definitionFit: To stagger or sway unsteadily, as when dizzy.

clue.text: Non-vegetarian, I'm allowed to eat one?

definitions.text: Non-vegetarian, I'm allowed to eat one?

indicators.note: the words Non-vegetarian, I'm allowed eat (contain) the answer within them

explanation.surface: A meat-eater declares that eating a beast is permitted.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across vegetariAN, I'M, ALlowed; read as a whole the clue also describes what a meat-eater may eat.
explanation.definitionFit: A creature from the fauna kingdom is what someone who eats meat is permitted to consume.

clue.text: Head, primarily sort to show consideration

indicators.note: primarily says the word for sort comes first in the answer

parts.note: kind means sort or type
a ness is a headland, a promontory

explanation.surface: A head teacher, above all, should show some thoughtfulness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'primarily' places KIND ahead of NESS, even though 'Head' comes first in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing thoughtfulness for others' feelings is a gentle, caring quality.

clue.text: Six geese on the loose? Explanation required

indicators.note: on the loose means running wild, so these letters are set free into a new order

explanation.surface: Six geese have escaped, and somebody needs to account for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the loose' rearranges SIX and GEESE.
explanation.definitionFit: Critical interpretation of a text, especially scripture, sets out its meaning.
